LD 44, An Act to Amend the Laws Pertaining to Elver Fishing

A

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources

Senator Tepler and colleagues on the Marine Resources Committee. I am Allison Hepler and I represent the towns of Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich. I am here
today to present LD 44, An Act to Amend the Laws Pertaining to Elver Fishing.

This is a Department of Marine Resources (DMR) bill and I am grateful to sponsor it. The goal of LD 44 has always been to enhance the security and integrity of Maine's elver fishery but, as
most of you know, the proposed content of this bill has changed dramatically since it was first published, in large part due to what we've come to expect in Maine's marine fisheries -- valuable
outreach and robust input. Rep. Simmons, Rep. Strout and I attended one such meeting last
month at DMR in a room filled beyond capacity with elver fishermen and DMR staff. The results
of that discussion you will see in the Department's amended version of this bill.

Thank you.

185856:
TESTIMONY OF
Patrick Keliher
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
In Support of
LD 44 An Act to Amend the Laws Pertaining to Elver Fishing
Before the Committee on Marine Resources Sponsored by Representative Hepler Date of Hearing: March 13, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Patrick Keliher, Commissioner of the Department of Marine Resources, and l am testifying on behalf of the Department in support of LD 44. This is a Department bill and we are
grateful to Representative Hepler for sponsoring it on our behalf.
While our testimony today is in support of the bill, the Department is requesting the committee's support in withdrawing Sections 1 and 5. Section 1 would have amended the existing penalty for selling elvers without using a swipe card from permanent revocation for the first offense, to 3 years for the first offense and permanent for the second offense, consistent with many other elver violations. However, at an industry meeting held in late January, it was the consensus position of the room that the existing penalty should remain.
Section 5 ofthe bill would have created a new prohibition on holding elvers in a residential dwelling, as
well as a prohibition on elver harvesters holding elvers for longer than 6 hours. The goal of this proposal was to minimize potential dead loss associated with holding elvers for long periods of time. However, at that same January industry meeting, harvesters expressed grave concern on the impacts of such a provision, including on price. They proposed alternative means of minimizing dead loss, as
well as ensuring that any minimal dead loss that may occur does not cause Maine to exceed the quota allocated to the state by ASMFC. Specifically, industry members suggested mandatory video training for new license holders to teach best handling practices, and the withholding of a small amount of
quota as a buffer. The Department has provided example language with this testimony for your
consideration.
'
The other elements of the bill are proposed to move forward, including moving the deadline for conducting the elver lottery from February 15 to March 15 to ensure ample time for lottery
administration. Finally, the bill would allow the holder of an elver fishing license to have another
license holder empty the fyke net when under the direct supervision of the license holder whose tag is on the net. Currently the ability to empty the fyke net is limited to the license holder whose tag is on the net, or an unlicensed crew member. Last season we heard from a number of license holders requesting additional flexibility in who can empty their fyke net under their direct supervision. This is
also the topic of Representative Strout's bill, LD 816 which the Department also supports.
Thank you for your consideration and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Ted Robinson Sedgwick LD 44
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Marine Resources Committee, my name is Ted Robinson. I am a Elver fisherman from Sedgwick Maine. Today, I would like to offer testimony against LD LD 44, "An Act to Amend the Laws Pertaining to Elver Fishing." I understand that the new law restricts fisherman to a limit of 6 hours to hold their eels before selling. I also understand that DMR has promised to remove that language from the bill, as this legislation would be disastrous for seller and buyer. Most fisherman babysit their eels better than their own children. We change the water every few days, check water temperature and pick out a handful of weak or sickly eels that never would have made it to China. This gives the buyer a better product and less dead loss in the buyers tanks. We hold our eels as leverage to get the price we want. If we can't hold eels we loose this leverage. I also heard that the 6 hour limit was a scare tactic to get fisherman to the table to motivate them to a lesser restriction. I would say such a tactic is disrespectful and manipulative. Why not develop minimum standards and training for holding eels and limiting dead loss. Treat us with dignity and respect, peers working together. Personally I never hold eels more than 3 weeks. I let them go and catch fresh ones to replace them. Also I have never had to hold them more than a month to get my target price. I don't believe any new legislation is needed. Let us have the freedom to fish according to the current laws and sell our eels according to the current laws. If DMR id worried about dead loss, put together a joint fisherman/biologist booked on eel care and give us the respect that most of us care about the eels and the fishery, and that we are doing our best to limit dead loss and provide a quality product to the buyer. Thank you.

My name is Timmy LaRochelle and l am an elver fisherman since 1994 before there was an actual
elver license.
I am a member of the ASMFC Advisory Panel, along with my colleague Sara adamaker of American
Unagi, who operates Maine's first full scale eel fann.
l own shares in Maine Eel Trade and Aquaculture (META).
And I was recently appointed as the Executive Director of the Maine Elver Fishermen's Association
(MEFA).
To put it mildly, l have a very strong, vested interest in the Maine glass eel fishery.
Since 2011, Maine's glass eel harvests have brought over $240 million dollars to Maine economy, making our fishery the second or third highest grossing in the state most years-
Maine ships 95% to 100% of its eels to China to be fann raised in ponds to % to 1 lb. in
weight. These eels are then processed in Chinese factories into high-value sushi products
that we import back at almost ten times the cost of the raw materials vve shipped to them in
the first place. -Eel farming and processing could be a half billion-dollar annual industry in North America!
With help from the state of Maine, our industry is ready to step-up and start getting that "value add" by raising and processing these eels in our own state and country.
American Unagi has already begun this effort and is collaborating with META's afliliates to make sure we can all compete effectively against any other country in the world in this industry.
But everything we do relies on stable quotas and a sustainable industry. This is the
foundation of the entire industry.
i am here today to support DMR's proposed legislation and to thank the Department for working with
the harvesters to create bills that are fair and reasonabie.
On behalf of MEFA, META and many or my industry colleagues, l also want to recognize our
outgoing Commissioner Pat Keliher for more than a decade of service to Maine's fisheries and fairminded support to the glass eel and lobster industries.
l also want to welcome the incoming Commissioner to his new position.
MEFA looks forward to a new era in its relations with the Department, the legislature and the
Governor's office on all issues related to this important fishery, both in the state and before the
ASMFC.
Wishing all harvesters a safe and successful season!
